title: Sri Lanka revises guidelines for appointment of President’s Counsel - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka has revised the guidelines governing the appointment of President’s Counsel, introducing a minimum 20-year professional experience requirement for eligible Attorneys-at-Law.

The revised guidelines were issued through Gazette Extraordinary No. 2498/76 dated July 24, 2026, under the direction of the President in terms of Article 33(e) of the Constitution.

The Gazette repeals and replaces Guideline No. 4 of the existing guidelines published in Gazette Extraordinary No. 2255/24 on November 24, 2021.

Under the revised guideline, an Attorney-at-Law will be eligible for appointment as a President’s Counsel only if he or she has been enrolled as an Attorney-at-Law of the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka for a minimum of 20 years.

The Gazette was issued by the Presidential Secretariat and signed by Secretary to the President Dr. N. S. Kumanayake.

Meanwhile, applications have been invited for the appointment of President’s Counsel for 2026. Eligible Attorneys-at-Law are required to submit their applications on or before August 31, 2026.

title: At least 35 killed in Syria bus collision, health ministry says - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
(The Times of Israel) - Thirty-five people were killed and 30 injured in a collision between two passenger buses on Syria’s Deir al-Zor-Damascus road, a health ministry official tells state news agency SANA.

The collision involved a bus carrying members of the Internal Security Forces and a civilian passenger bus, state news agency SANA reports, citing the interior ministry.

title: Cassilingham receives appointment as SLPP Jaffna District Organizer - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror): Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) Politburo Member G. Cassilingham today officially received his letter of appointment as the party’s Jaffna District Organizer from SLPP National Organiser Namal Rajapaksa at the party headquarters on Nelum Mawatha in Colombo.

The appointment reflects the party leadership’s confidence in Cassilingham as the SLPP continues to strengthen its organisational network in the Northern Province.

title: Cockroach Janta Party calls off protest after Indian govt meets demands - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
(The Business Standard) - The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) today (25 July) withdrew its protest against exam paper leaks after the Indian government accepted all its demands, following 36 days of demonstrations.

CJP spokesperson Saurav Das announced the decision at a joint press conference in New Delhi after the third round of talks between the party delegation and the government.

"The CJP declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith and understanding that the agreed upon terms will be executed within the agreed upon timeline," Das said.

He made the announcement alongside federal ministers Jitendra Singh and JP Nadda.

Another CJP spokesperson, Ashutosh Ranka, said the government had accepted all their demands after the prolonged protest.

"We urge everyone to peacefully withdraw from the protest sites," he added.

title: Jaffna Kings franchise agreement terminated over alleged integrity breaches - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) has announced that the Jaffna Kings franchise agreement in the Lanka Premier League (LPL) has been terminated following alleged breaches of anti-corruption and integrity provisions.

In a statement issued on July 25, 2026, SLC said it had been informed by the LPL Event Rights Partner, Innovative Production Group FZ LLC (IPG), that it had exercised its contractual right to terminate the Jaffna Kings Franchise Agreement.

Under the LPL Event Rights Agreement, IPG will assume responsibility for all obligations of the Jaffna franchise, including settling outstanding payments due to players and fulfilling all other contractual commitments of the franchise.

Sri Lanka Cricket reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding the integrity of the Lanka Premier League and said it maintains a strict zero-tolerance policy towards corruption and any conduct that compromises, or has the potential to compromise, the integrity of the game.

SLC said it would continue working with all stakeholders to ensure the highest standards of governance, transparency and integrity are maintained throughout the LPL.

title: Nine arrested after attack on Wildlife and STF officers in Kilinochchi - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - A group of individuals has been arrested for obstructing the duties of Wildlife and Police Special Task Force (STF) personnel and launching an attack on them during a raid in Akkarayankulam, Kilinochchi.

The confrontation occurred when a joint team of Wildlife and STF officers conducted a raid in the Mukkanpan area of Akkarayankulam. The operation was initiated following a tip-off regarding the illegal clearing of a local forest reserve.

According to the police, individuals present at the location obstructed the officers from carrying out their duties and proceeded to assault them. As the unrest escalated, STF personnel were forced to fire warning shots into the air to bring the volatile situation under control.

Four STF officers who sustained injuries during the clash were admitted to the Kilinochchi Hospital for medical treatment.

Authorities have since stabilized the situation, confirming the arrest of nine suspects in connection with the violent obstruction. Police said that one of the arrested individuals was also hospitalized due to a sudden medical condition.

In addition to the arrests, they seized the heavy machinery used by the suspects to illegally clear the protected reserve. The Akkarayankulam Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.

title: Tharoor, Mano discuss Indo-Lanka ties, regional cooperation and democratic governance - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Acclaimed author, parliamentarian and Chairman of India’s Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs, Dr. Shashi Tharoor MP, held a cordial and substantive meeting with Tamil Progressive Alliance Leader and Member of Parliament Mano Ganesan and TPA Vice President for International Relations Barath Arullsamy during his recent visit to Colombo.

Mano Ganesan and Arullsamy paid a courtesy call on Dr. Tharoor, during which they exchanged views on Sri Lanka–India relations, regional political developments, cultural ties and opportunities for deeper cooperation between the two neighbouring nations.

Dr. Tharoor, a four-term Member of Parliament representing Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala and one of India’s most celebrated authors and public intellectuals, discussed the strategic importance of regional connectivity, transshipment and closer economic engagement between India and Sri Lanka.

Mano Ganesan highlighted the longstanding relationship between India and Sri Lanka and the importance of continued engagement concerning the aspirations of the Indian Origin Tamil community, while strengthening wider people-to-people and cultural relations.

The discussion also covered the emerging common platform of Tamil-speaking political parties in Sri Lanka and its role in advancing democratic dialogue, constitutional reform and inclusive national development.

Dr. Tharoor further shared insights into the functioning of India’s Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs, including the contribution of parliamentary committees and opposition legislators to policy oversight and democratic governance.

In a gracious gesture, Dr. Tharoor presented Mano Ganesan with an authentic Kerala shawl, adding warmth and cultural significance to the occasion. 

Speaking after the meeting, Arullsamy said it was a distinct privilege to engage with one of the most distinguished alumni of St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, noting that he too is an alumnus of the institution. He noted that their shared Stephanian connection made the meeting personally meaningful, while discussions also touched on future academic, alumni and leadership initiatives involving the St. Stephen’s community in Sri Lanka.

Arullsamy described the meeting as warm, intellectually enriching and forward-looking, reflecting the enduring importance of continued dialogue between Sri Lanka and India.

title: CAA, STF seize expired fertilizer stock in Kaduwela raid - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA), together with the Police Special Task Force (STF), has seized a stock of expired fertilizers that had allegedly been secretly stored in lorries by an institution in the Bomiriya area of Kaduwela.

The raid was carried out on the evening of July 21 by the CAA and the STF's Special Operations Unit No. 01.

During the operation, officials recovered 376 kilograms of expired solid fertilizers and 1,170 litres of expired liquid fertilizers.

The seized fertilizer stock has been taken into the custody of the Consumer Affairs Authority and sealed, while further investigations are underway.

The CAA said legal action will be instituted against the institution concerned once investigations are completed.

The authority also urged consumers and farmers to report any information regarding substandard, expired or misleadingly marketed products by contacting its 1977 hotline during office hours.

title: Paddy cultivators stage protest in Anuradhapura - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Dayaratne Embogama

Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Paddy cultivators in the Anuradhapura District yesterday staged a protest in Anuradhapura town against the poor guaranteed price for paddy and demanded a minimum price of Rs.150 per kilo.

More than 1,000 farmers affiliated to Nuwarawewa, Nachchaduwa, Thissawewa, Padaviya, Wahalkara, Mahakanadarawa, Huruluwsewa, Rajangana and Wilachchiya farmer organisations participated.

President of Anuradhapura District Farmer Organisation Collective Punchirala Ratnayaka said the farmers staged protests in their areas and, as a last resort, gathered in Anuradhapura to stage this massive protest.

“We made continual representations to the Government, the Minister of Agriculture and Deputy Minister to increase the guaranteed price for paddy but to no avail. We are determined to continue our campaign. The government held talks with the rice mill owners and decided on a guaranteed price of Rs.120, but the rice mill owners pay only Rs. 80 per kilo. Although we had a bumper harvest in the Yala season, we are facing hardship for want of a remunerative market for paddy,” he said.

title: Farewell Ambassador Qi Zhenhong of China! - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Prof. Samitha Hettige

Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka has always been a global trading hub and as result many Envoy appointments are recorded through its long history. Among notable envoys recorded are Emperor Ashoka's Envoys (3rd Century BC), Persian Envoys (2nd Century BC), Roman Envoys (1st Century AD), Chinese Buddhist Scholars (5th Century AD) and Chinese Admiral Zheng He (14th Century AD). Assistance provided by Admiral Zheng He is recorded in the trilingual plaque on display at the national museum in Colombo.

Among notable Sri Lankan Envoys are; trader brothers Thapassu and Balluka (who met the Buddha), Envoys of King Mahanama in China and Rome (1st Century AD) and Ambassador Jayapala of Chilaw in Great China during the Ming Dynasty (14th Century AD). Jayapala is believed to have travelled to China on 6 occasions. It was the peak of the maritime Silk Road when Sri Jayawardenepura became capital under Parakramabahu VI who resided close to ‘Mirihana’ in Jayawardenepura. Above indicates that Sino Lanka diplomatic ties have been stronger than most of Sri Lanka’s bilateral relations.

Term of Ambassador Qi Zhenhong

Ambassador Qi Zhenhong arrived in Sri Lanka in late 2020 when Sri Lanka was combating COVID – 19 under President Gotabaya who ruled the country from Mirihana. Sri Lankans may remember the simple arrival ceremony Chinese Embassy held on advice of Ambassador Qi Zhenhong respecting the health guidelines of Sri Lanka to prevent the spread of COVID – 19.

Ambassador Qi was one of the first to organise free COVID vaccines for Sri Lankans. He will have special memories about Sri Lanka as he witnessed; Sri Lankans fighting COVID -19, mismanaging and re-energising the economy, the peoples uprising (Aragalaya) and the rule of three Executive Presidents. Sri Lankans celebrated the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Peoples Republic of China and Sri Lanka in 2022. In the same year the 70th anniversary of signing the Rubber Rice Pact with China was also marked. China is revisiting the ancient Silk Road for global human development with the four global initiatives (Global Security Initiative, Global Governance Initiative, Global Civilisation Initiative and the Global Development Initiative) supported by the Belt and Road Initiative. As the UN General Assembly has endorsed these initiatives, it is important for Sri Lanka to get more involved with those to re-energise the economy.

Safe journey dear Ambassador!

title: Five people injured after elephant attacks van - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Five people were injured when an elephant attacked a van travelling from Padukka to Anuradhapura yesterday.

It was reported that the van had knocked the animal a few metres before it reached the spot where the tragedy struck.

The injured were admitted to hospital. The condition of three people was said to be serious. Some six people were travelling in the van, according to police.

The village of Padeniya in Anuradhapura District is said to have suffered because of wild elephants during the past few years. Around 20 people have died as a result of human-elephant conflict in the area.

title: I will come back to Parliament in 2029 and make sure that Minister Harshana Nanayakkara in prison: Archchuna - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara was asleep after a booze at the time of the clash in Negombo Prison, Independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna alleged in Parliament yesterday.

“The Minister was not aware of what was going on,” he said.

“I will come to Parliament in 2029 as well and will see to it that Minister Nanayakkara is sent to Prison,” he added.

Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe who responded said the Justice Minister having a drink is his personal business. “These MPs speak as if they put soda into the Minister's drink. The Minister performed his duty after the clash. He did everything for the victims of the clash,” he said.
